title: Piri Piri Chicken
subtitle: Portuguese chilli chicken with lemon and garlic
excerpt: Portugal's most famous chicken dish: spatchcocked chicken marinated in a fiery paste of piri piri chilli, lemon, garlic, and smoked paprika, then grilled or roasted until charred, smoky, and outrageously juicy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Piri piri chicken (also peri-peri) has its origins in the Portuguese colonisation of Africa, specifically Mozambique and Angola, where Portuguese settlers used the African bird's eye chilli (piri piri in Swahili, meaning 'pepper pepper') in their cooking. The dish became particularly associated with the Algarve region of Portugal, where restaurants serving spatchcocked chicken marinated in piri piri sauce and cooked over charcoal became a national institution. The dish was further popularised internationally by the Nando's restaurant chain. A good piri piri marinade balances the heat of the chilli with garlic, smoked paprika, lemon, and a little vinegar. Spatchcocking (removing the backbone and flattening) is essential for even cooking on the grill or under the oven grill.

content.text: Marinate overnight if possible; even 4 hours makes a significant difference to the depth of flavour. Spatchcock the chicken by cutting along both sides of the backbone with kitchen scissors and pressing flat; this halves the cooking time and produces a more evenly cooked result. The chicken should char slightly in places; this is desirable, not a mistake.

items.preparation: spatchcocked: backbone removed and pressed flat
bird's eye chillies; or 3 for medium heat

content.text: Blend the chillies, garlic, lemon juice and zest, smoked paprika, olive oil, vinegar, salt, pepper, and thyme to a smooth paste. Score the chicken all over with a sharp knife through to the bone. Pour the marinade over and work it into the cuts. Marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours.

Preheat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7, or heat a barbecue to high. Roast the chicken flat in a roasting tin for 40 to 45 minutes, basting with pan juices halfway through, until cooked through and charred in places (74°C internal). Or grill over a hot barbecue for 20 to 25 minutes per side.
Rest for 10 minutes. Serve with chips, salad, and any remaining marinade warmed as a sauce.
